title: What starts the Great Whirl
query: The Great Whirl, the large anticyclone that forms off Somalia each summer, has been attributed both to the local southwest-monsoon winds and to planetary (Rossby) waves that reach the coast before the monsoon starts. Using the supplied GLORYS12 monthly sea surface height, velocity, temperature and salinity for 2011-2020 in the western and northern Arabian Sea (47-70 E, 4-26 N), determine when and where the Great Whirl forms, intensifies and decays in each year, how variable it is, and which proposed initiation mechanism the data support. Winds are not supplied.
